create.name: Vedanta Society of Toronto
create.bio:
The Vedanta Society of Toronto is a branch of the Ramakrishna Order and was the Order's first centre in Canada. Swami Ranganathananda inaugurated it in November 1968 at a gathering in downtown Toronto, with Swami Bhashyananda of Chicago presiding, and it now has its own red-roofed temple on Emmett Avenue in the city's west end. Swami Pramathananda led it from 1989 to 2003, and Swami Kripamayananda, a former schoolmaster in the Order's Indian schools, has been minister in charge since 2003. The society also keeps in touch with smaller Vedanta groups in Ottawa, Calgary and Winnipeg.

Teaching follows the Ramakrishna–Vivekananda tradition: a single reality behind everything, a divine core in each person, and respect for every faith. Every evening there is a vesper service with chanting, singing and a reading from the Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna, followed by half an hour of meditation. Sunday morning talks and a Friday evening scripture class, lately on the Uddhava Gita, are streamed and kept on its YouTube channel, and a monthly day-long vigil of japa and meditation is held at the temple. Vedanta Vidya Mandir, a Sunday school started in 2003, gives children moral and spiritual education online and in person, and members volunteer at a soup kitchen and food bank.

free_resources.title: Vespers, Meditation and Sunday Talks
free_resources.description: The temple's regular round: an evening vesper service with chanting and a Gospel reading, followed by meditation; Sunday morning lectures; and a monthly dawn-to-dusk vigil of japa and meditation.

free_resources.title: Vedanta Vidya Mandir
free_resources.description: A Sunday school, now in its 23rd year, offering moral and spiritual education for children from kindergarten to high school, online and at the ashram. Registration opens each August.
